Subject: [DataSage] CPPO entitlement duplication detected — need mapping help

Alex / team,

We started provisioning the Channel Partner Private Offer for DataSage (deal 98321) and noticed what looks like duplicated entitlement rows in AWS Producer Console. The partner portal shows two SKUs that appear to map to the same internal product ("datasage-core-v1"). AWS is rejecting the entitlement submission until we resolve the duplication.

Attached is the CSV we exported from the portal (entitlement-mapping.csv) — you can see the duplicate external SKU values in columns E/F, and two different billing entities are listed in column H. DataSage needs CPPO active by 2026-09-05 to meet their procurement window.

Can Redwood confirm which SKU we should use (single consolidated SKU vs. keep both and split billing)? Also need confirmation on the invoice entity mapping and whether we should create two distinct entitlements on your side.

Short turnaround on this — happy to jump on a quick call.

Attachments: entitlement-mapping.csv (CSV, 28KB)

Thanks,
Lara Owen

Subject: Re: [DataSage] CPPO entitlement duplication detected — need mapping help

Thanks Lara — got the CSV and have sketched a quick plan. A couple clarifying Qs before we proceed:

- Do both external SKUs represent materially different entitlements (feature gates / support tiers), or are they duplicate rows that should collapse to the same unit?
- Which billing entity does DataSage want invoices to be issued to (their parent vs. EU subsidiary shown in your file)?

Tentative plan from our side:
1) If the SKUs are identical in capability, we prefer collapsing to a single entitlement to avoid confusion in CPPO activation.
2) If legal / invoicing requires two entities, we can create two entitlements with the same technical mapping but different invoice entity tags — need procurement PO and entity tax IDs to set that up.
3) If AWS still rejects, we'll create a short-lived workaround: create a secondary internal SKU that points to the same model bundle but routes invoices to the alternate entity.

Ben / Marissa — FYI: Ben, could you confirm DataSage's invoicing preference with your contact? Marissa, will you coordinate with Partner Ops if we need to create a second entitlement?

I can be on a call at 11:30am PT today if that works for you.

— Alex

> Alex / team,
>
> We started provisioning the Channel Partner Private Offer for DataSage (deal 98321) and noticed what looks like duplicated entitlement rows in AWS Producer Console.

Quick update from procurement side: DataSage prefers single invoice to parent entity (DataSage Analytics, US HQ). They requested we do not split invoices across subsidiaries. That makes things simpler — collapse to a single external SKU if possible.

If you need a workaround for AWS acceptance, here's what worked for another partner: we create an internal alias SKU (internal-sku-<deal>) that references the primary product and then push both external SKUs to that alias for the marketplace submission. Once CPPO is active we reconcile the alias mapping on our side and issue a single invoice to the parent.

I'm attaching a proposed mapping workbook with suggested alias names and accounting tags (proposed-mapping.xlsx).

Action items for Ops:
- Alex: confirm alias approach and align 1:1 mapping on Redwood side.
- Priyom: if we go alias route, can you update entitlement provisioning scripts to accept alias_sku and invoice_entity fields?
- Lara: confirm AWS will accept aliasing for CPPO submission; if not, notify and we'll pivot.

Ben

Thanks Ben — yes, DataSage confirms single invoice to parent is preferred. AWS Marketplace Support indicated that aliasing is acceptable provided the alias points to the same product bundle and the CPPO request documents the rationale. They did flag settlement splitting as "manual" — so if invoices are split, settlement will require a separate accounting ticket and could delay payment runs.

We attached DataSage PO for the first commit (PO_78923.pdf). They asked whether the invoice should reference the alias SKU or the external SKU in the invoice line items.

Next steps we need from Redwood:
- Final alias name agreed (so we can submit CPPO)
- Confirmation that Redwood will reconcile alias -> primary SKU post-activation and that invoicing will be to DataSage parent entity.
- DocuSign-ready contract with CPPO clause (if possible).

Availability: we can do 30 min call tomorrow 9am PT.

Attachments: PO_78923.pdf (PDF, 45KB)

Best,
Lara Owen

- DataSage wants single invoice to US parent.
- AWS accepts aliasing with documentation; settlement splitting is manual and we should avoid it.
- Proposed alias: "rdw-ds-98321-alias-v1" (we'll use this in the CPPO submission).

Runbook (short):
1) Redwood creates internal alias sku "rdw-ds-98321-alias-v1" pointing to same product bundle.
2) Ben confirms alias in HubSpot (https://app.hubspot.com/deals/98321) and we include alias in CPPO request notes.
3) CloudResell submits CPPO with alias and attached PO_78923.pdf; AWS will accept but ops flagged settlement manual.
4) Upon CPPO activation, Priyom will run reconciliation script to map alias -> primary SKU and close the accounting ticket.
5) Alex to upload final signed CPPO contract to Drive and share DocuSign receipt link (https://www.docusign.net/receipt?docusign_id=ABC123-CPPO).

Action owners and deadlines:

- Priyom: prepare entitlement script changes and test in staging (due 2026-08-30).
- Ben: confirm with HubSpot entry and DataSage contact (done).
- Lara / CloudResell: submit CPPO to AWS and confirm acceptance (aiming for 2026-08-31).
